text:
the idea that the future of work is still agile kanban is so fucking disappointing.

“yeah, the model smashes the narrow SAT-esque benchmark, it’s probably near-AGI… anyway, we somehow made a worse Asana. now watch your coworkers babysit their agents too.”

OpenAI shouldn’t be stuck doing weird ui/os stuff, it’s cool, but they’re one of the few companies capable of chasing exponentially more brilliant models. there should be an ecosystem downstream creating enough computation and money that this isn’t necessary. 

founders, builders, funds need to make horizontal innovation an expectation across the rest of the stack, rather than settling for vertical products harvesting marginal gains from the latest model- it’s a cancer; everything is neatly categorised into a frontier derivative that predictably improves NPS by a small margin. 

Apple beat Microsoft by refusing to accept that better underlying technology was enough. they innovated across UX, systems engineering, components and design.

we should expect the same ambition from the rest of the AI stack.

text:
The OpenAI team just shared a video introducing ChatGPT Space, and it stands out because it features the actual people building the feature rather than polished presenters.

ChatGPT Space is a shared workspace inside ChatGPT where teams keep pages, files, and related work in one place.

Users can write and edit documents alongside ChatGPT or personal agents called dots, then invite others to view, comment, or collaborate in real time.

It replaces the previous Library feature and is currently available to Pro, Business, and Enterprise plan users on web and desktop.

The video walks through how pages support research, charts, images, and other content that both people and AI can update together.

Just yesterday the team added slides support so collaborators can build presentations directly in the same environment.

Sharing is private by default, with options to grant access to specific people, teams, or entire workspaces while keeping clear boundaries.

The post notes the demo feels endearingly awkward at times simply because the real product team is on camera.

They close by asking what features people want to see next as they continue rolling out improvements.

text:
Tibo, are Plus users not worth learning from? 🙃
Pro gets it first again, and this time Plus has to wait in line just to make a slide deck lol
Tibo just dropped an intro video for ChatGPT Space. It's the actual team on camera, so it's a little awkward in a cute way, and he's asking what we want next. Total manager energy.
Space launched on 10/14. It's a shared workspace where your team writes and edits docs together with ChatGPT.
He also mentioned slides support just got added, but only for Pro, Business and Enterprise for now, because they want to learn from feedback first.
Not hating on the feature itself. Someone in the replies already called it Notion without the databases. But leaving Plus out every single time is getting old 🫠
